extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: An evaluation benchmark for low-resource and multilingual machine translation. It consists of 3001 sentences sampled from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages, enabling many-to-many multilingual evaluation with multilingually aligned translations.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources, specifically English Wikipedia, Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage. The sentence selection process involved randomly selecting an article from each source and manually selecting a few contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding very short or malformed sentences. For each sentence, the Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags for linked entities and images were also recorded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia-derived text from multiple Wikimedia sources: Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage; source sentences were public, freely available text under permissive licensing.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentence selection was done by manually selecting a few contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding very short or malformed sentences, and selecting one paragraph per document from the beginning, middle, or end. The selection process was performed by 10 annotators in the lab, and all sentences were manually labeled by sub-topic.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 10 annotators in the lab: 6 male and 4 female; researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark has broader topic coverage than existing datasets, but the paper notes that many existing low-resource MT benchmarks have very low coverage of languages, are domain-specific, or are built using automatic approaches, which can bias evaluation toward certain languages/domains and lower-quality data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is an evaluation benchmark, not a training corpus. The paper emphasizes that low-resource MT evaluation is difficult because high-quality data are scarce, existing benchmarks have limited language coverage, and many are domain-specific or low quality. It also notes that professional translators are scarce and their work is hard to quality-check. The dataset is intended for evaluation of translation and related tasks, not as a general-purpose dataset for all uses.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as beneficial for improving translation systems for low-resource languages, which could help the majority of the world's population who speak such languages. The paper frames the social impact as enabling better translation quality, broader language access, and support for community efforts and shared tasks.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language and geography are explicitly involved through the 101 languages covered and low-resource language communities; the paper also mentions multilingual domain adaptation and document-level translation, but does not explicitly state collection of other sensitive human attributes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use is evaluation/benchmarking for machine translation, especially many-to-many multilingual translation across 10,100 language pairs. The paper also says it can be used for sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation. It is intended for shared tasks and community evaluation efforts.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state an intention to continue expanding the number of languages covered and to make the test set available to community efforts, but no explicit versioning schedule, maintainer list, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We manually selected a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. To avoid bias coming from the document structure, we carefully selected one paragraph per document, from either the beginning, middle or end of the article. We balanced the location selection to be equally distributed across the whole corpus — roughly one third of paragraphs were sampled from the beginning of the article, one third from the middle, and so on.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “These often have very low coverage of low-resource languages... limiting our understanding of how well methods generalize and scale to a larger number of languages with a diversity of linguistic features.
